newsitem.title: USA: Citicorp loses legal round in Lloyd's case.
newsitem.headline: Citicorp loses legal round in Lloyd's case.

text.p: A U.S. court has denied part of Citibank's motion to dismiss a lawsuit that alleges a unit of the bank mishandled trust funds of the Lloyd's of London insurance market, court papers have showed.
The suit, filed by U.S. investors in Lloyd's, is one of countless court actions prompted by the collapse of the Lloyd's market in the 1980s that resulted in billions of dollars of losses.

On January 24, Judge Robert Sweet of the U.S. District court for the Southern District of New York allowed the case to go forward in New York, after finding for Citibank on one of its claims but ruling against the bank on other claims.
Sweet has yet to rule on whether to certify the suit as a class action.

Sweet ruled in a 65-page written opinion that Citibank could not invoke certain clauses in the contracts between Lloyd's and its investors, known as "Names," that say disputes must be litigated in Britain.

The judge instructed attorneys for the plaintiffs to amend the complaint to include in the definition of a class all Names who underwrote American business. Plaintiffs' attorneys were also told to submit additional facts "related to their request for an injuncton prohibiting Citibank from transferring funds to Lloyd's."

A spokesman for the plaintiffs said that under Sweet's order, the group's complaint will be amended to include in the class definition all Names, including non-U.S. and U.S. citizens, who have participated in Lloyd's American insurance business.
